text:
anna: quick postmortem note from this morning's flapping incident. multiple candidate routes collapsed to identical normalized buckets -> churn.

kevin: saw it. cluster-level tie means deterministic selection fell back to list order and picked a tiny zone repeatedly. not ideal.

sara: what collapsed them? bucketization granularity? cost slope?

anna: a combination: score normalization -> quantize to 8 bins -> winsorize -> apply region penalty -> final normalize. quantize step lost the small deltas between routes.

liam: two quick asks: (1) we need a cheap deterministic tie-breaker in the policy evaluator, (2) instrument how often ties occur.

kevin: proposal: evaluator receives an extra 16-bit tie_key per route from compiler. comparator tuple = (bucket_id, cost_rank, p95_latency_rank, tie_key). compare lexicographically.

sara: sounds okay. can the tie_key be stable across hot reloads and config churn? we can't have it change on every deployment.

kevin: yes, tie_key = low16(xxh3_64(route_id) xor consider(region_shard)). compiler assigns it when policy is compiled and stores in the route manifest. stable until policy recompile.

anna: nice. also add a small per-tenant comparator_spec in policy metadata to let latency-first tenants prefer (bucket, p95_latency_rank, cost_rank, tie_key). default remains cost-first. must be opt-in.

liam: perf constraints: comparator must be O(1) with tiny memory. target < 200ns per route comparison on x86. keep fields as uint16 to help vectorized compares.

kevin: implementation note for compiler: emit compressed route tuple into runtime proto as four uint16s. runtime compares on tuple without extra allocations.

sara: add telemetry: policy.tie_resolutions.total, policy.tie_resolutions.by_field (bucket|cost|lat|tie_key), and policy.tie_resolutions.per_tenant. helps catch dominance.

anna: anti-flap: when comparator selects route with capacity < threshold (say 15% of max shard capacity), start a 30s soft-hold before switching again for that tenant. cooldown should be tunable by tenant policy (field: anti_flap_seconds).

liam: careful: avoid long holds that mask real regressions. default 30s, expose metric policy.flap_held.count. make it a soft suggestion to the decision path (i.e., comparator returns same route unless new candidate has bucket advantage >= 2).

kevin: test matrix: unit tests for lexicographic tie-break with synthetic routes, sim for the prod-capture case (small vs large vs europe), perf bench for comparator hot path, and compatibility test for legacy behavior when legacy_nondet_routing=true.

sara: rollout plan: behind ff tie_breaker_compiler_v2, unit+sim green, canary to 1% tenants for 24h (track flap_rate, p95 latency per-tenant, tie_resolutions), then 10% for 48h, then ramp.

anna: document migration: add policy migration guide and an escape hatch in console to toggle legacy_nondet_routing per-tenant for 2 weeks. operations to contact SRE if they see regressions.

policy-bot: created issue #PLAT-1482: "tie-breaker comparator + anti-flap rollout" and assigned to @kevin.

kevin: i'll open compiler PR today with emitted tie_key and comparator_spec proto. will include bench results.

liam: i'll add the telemetry dashboards and write the sim scenarios. thanks.

sara: small nit: pick default bin count carefully. 8 bins may be too coarse for some workloads. propose default 16 with runtime override.

anna: agreed. default 16, but keep config in policy metadata with safe bounds (4..256). document recommended values.

kevin: noted. i'll include that in RFC addendum.

anna: great work. let's sync tomorrow AM to review PR + sim outputs.

liam: +1.

sara: thanks everyone :rocket:
